newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen in listless range, seen top-heavy.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen in listless range, seen top-heavy.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures were higher in late Thursday trade but dealers said the market lacked conviction on the upside, limiting scope for further gains.

They said activity was slow and rangebound due to a dearth of fresh leads and caution ahead of Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls report, which will be monitored for signals to U.S. and Japanese interest rate policy.
"There are a lot of good buyers of December Euroyen out in the low 98.70s. But for now, we're in no-man's land," a dealer with a U.S. futures house said.
He said the contract would face selling pressure around 98.92/94, but looked supported near its day low of 98.83. It stood at 98.86 at 1125 GMT against an IMM close at 98.86.

A trader at a Japanese brokerage said Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures weakened in early trade on reports Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita had said the central bank was ready to take pre-emptive action, when necessary, in steering monetary policy.
"The market reacted, but it looks like it was a calm reaction," the trader said, adding that a break below 98.83 could take December Euroyen as low as 98.75.

"I'd think of selling on rallies because it looks like the people who are suffering under the low rate regime, like retirees, are putting more pressure (on politicians) to ask for higher rates," he added.
September JGBs ended at 122.71 against their previous 122.72 with activity driven by players rolling over their positions ahead of June's expiry on Friday.
Eurodollar futures slipped a notch in thin trade, with December ending at 93.780 against its IMM close at 93.795 on volume of 4,020 lots.
Weekly jobless claims figures, due at 1230 GMT, were expected to generate little interest ahead of Friday's jobs number.
